submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis found a small depressive-symptom signal with DHEA, but GRADE certainty was very low.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found a small pooled improvement in depressive symptoms with DHEA versus placebo across heterogeneous psychiatric and medical populations. The evidence was rated very low certainty by GRADE, and influential studies affected heterogeneity. This supports a tentative indication-specific signal rather than a general mood or anti-aging recommendation.
submissions.populationContext: Mixed depression and medical-condition populations across randomized DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA treatment regimens varied across trials; endocrine context and dose remain source-specific.
submissions.safetyContext: Androgenic adverse effects were reported; hormonal conversion is relevant to safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very-low-certainty evidence cannot justify high-confidence public efficacy language. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: Pooled randomized-trial data show DHEA's bone/body-composition effects are sex-specific and track downstream sex-hormone changes.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A pooled analysis of four randomized clinical trials in adults aged 55 years and older found sex-specific effects of DHEA on hormones, bone mineral density and body composition. Changes in androgen and estrogen exposure differed between women and men, and observed BMD/body-composition responses were not uniform across sexes or skeletal sites. The evidence therefore cannot support a single generic anti-aging or bone-health effect.
submissions.populationContext: Older women and men across four randomized DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA replacement/supplementation in older adults; sex and baseline endocrine context are material.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Pooled trial data do not establish broad clinical-outcome benefit or suitability outside the studied older populations. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized-trial meta-analysis found partial BMD benefit mainly in women, not a consistent bone effect across older adults.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials found that DHEA replacement produced partial improvements in hip/trochanter bone mineral density in women, while comparable benefits were not observed consistently in men and clinically significant effects remained uncertain. Bone outcomes must therefore remain sex- and site-specific rather than becoming a generic DHEA bone-strength claim.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy older adults in randomized placebo-controlled DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA replacement; BMD site and sex materially alter interpretation.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: BMD surrogate changes do not establish fracture prevention or overall anti-aging benefit. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: In elderly men, DHEA showed no clear benefit across several clinical outcomes and a small fat-mass effect was explained by downstream sex-hormone changes.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A meta-analysis of placebo-controlled DHEA trials in elderly men found a small reduction in fat mass, but that association disappeared after accounting for DHEA-related increases in androgen/estrogen metabolites. No clear benefit was observed across several other outcomes including bone health, sexual function, quality of life, and lipid/glycemic measures. This directly constrains broad anti-aging claims in men.
submissions.populationContext: Elderly men across placebo-controlled DHEA trials.
submissions.usageContext: DHEA supplementation in older men; downstream hormonal conversion mediates interpretation.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome-specific nulls and endocrine mediation remain first-class. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live DHEA profile describes moderate human evidence and endocrine safety limits while exposing zero canonical receipts and unrestricted recommendation defaults.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current NOINDEX DHEA profile exposes sourceCount zero and no claim map while stating moderate human evidence and warning about androgenic effects and hormone-sensitive cancers. Those benefit and safety propositions require outcome-specific and safety-specific receipts before recommendation eligibility can be governed reliably. The profile should remain NOINDEX/needs-review while evidence, endocrine risk, and recommendation state reconcile.
submissions.usageContext: Repository evidence-receipt/governance gap; no public mutation in this fragment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This record does not independently determine final medical-risk classification or recommendation policy.
